page.layout: One printed page, cut off at its left edge. Top: running head "LIBER I." centred with page number at top right. Below: running text in lines of two paragraphs, cut at the left. Below the text: a woodcut diagram of a globe with sun positions, labels Septentrio, Meridies, Occasus, Umbra, Umbra sinistra, Umbra dextra, and "Septen" below the diagram at right.

main_text.p: [illegible, ~6 letters]dem intelligendum est de illis populis, qui habi-tant ad polum antarcticum.

Et tantum etiam de distinctione partium terrae respectu umbrarum Solis, de qua distinct. Lue Gauri-cus in sua Geographia ita perspicue tractat, ut non in-[illegible, ~6 letters] horizontis schemate etiam rem depingat.

page.notes: The left side of the page is cut off, so many line beginnings and ends are lost. The diagram labels are partly unclear: "Umbra" and "dextra" read with some uncertainty, and the word at the right of the middle sun is illegible. The label "Septen" at the lower right is a fragment. The page number is a printed numeral that reads roughly as 811 and is uncertain.
